name: grid_pickup
description: Copies an app you can see into your own grid as a new app.

arguments.name: entity_id
arguments.desc: The source app to copy: a canonical UUID or <grid-slug>/<entity-slug>.

arguments.name: grid
arguments.desc: Grid to create your copy in. Required only when you belong to more than one grid.

arguments.name: id
arguments.desc: Legacy alias of entity_id.

arguments.name: into_org_slug
arguments.desc: Legacy alias of grid.

arguments.name: name
arguments.desc: Slug for your copy. Omit to derive one from the source.

arguments.name: source_version_id
arguments.desc: Copy an older version instead of HEAD, e.g. v_a1b2c3d.

annotations.title: Copy an app into your grid

name: grid_pull
description: Fetches an app you can push to, so the next plug updates it.

arguments.name: claim_token
arguments.desc: Claiming a drop plugged outside a grid: its owner token, which claims that drop into your grid. Only the drop's owner can claim it.

arguments.name: claim_url
arguments.desc: Alternative to claim_token: the claim_url from the plug result; the token is read from it.

arguments.name: entity_id
arguments.desc: The entity id to pull. Defaults to the drop made outside a grid in this session, if any.

arguments.name: grid
arguments.desc: Grid to resolve a bare slug in. Required only when you belong to more than one grid.

annotations.title: Pull an app to edit in place

name: grid_collab
description: Asks for, or grants, push access to an app someone else owns.

arguments.name: entity_id
arguments.desc: The app to get push access to: a canonical UUID or <grid-slug>/<entity-slug>.

arguments.name: grid
arguments.desc: Grid to resolve a bare slug in. Required only when a bare slug is ambiguous across grids you belong to.

annotations.title: Get push access to an app you don't own

name: grid_create_grid
description: Creates a grid (workspace) after the user confirms its name.

arguments.name: slug
arguments.desc: The grid slug: 3-40 lowercase letters, digits, or hyphens, starting with a letter. Permanent: it appears in every app URL in the grid.

arguments.name: name
arguments.desc: Display name (defaults to the slug).

name: grid_note
description: Sends a build note the user asked for to the CloudGrid team.

arguments.name: summary
arguments.desc: A short plain-language note on what was built and why. This text is sent.

annotations.title: Send a build note to the CloudGrid team

name: grid_plug
description: Plugs a page or an app and returns its live URL; with a target it updates that app in place.

arguments.name: anon
arguments.desc: Deprecated and ignored: it does not publish. A new plug needs sign-in: without it the result is needs_auth and nothing is published, even with anon: true. Editing a drop that was plugged outside a grid takes target_entity_id + owner_token.

arguments.name: artifact_files
arguments.desc: The source inline, one entry per file, for hosted/no-filesystem transports (a multi-file app). A single HTML page fits `html`. Sent INLINE (copied through this call), so large files (lockfiles, binaries) can truncate and fail the build; for a real framework, a lockfile, or binary assets, the disk-based CLI (`npx -y @cloudgrid-io/cli plug` where it is already signed in) is more reliable. Mutually exclusive with `html` and `path`.

arguments.name: cloudgrid_yaml
arguments.desc: Inline cloudgrid.yaml (the entity manifest). Optional; server auto-detection applies when omitted. On re-plug, a name: change is a warning only; the entity keeps its name and URL.

arguments.name: confirm_new_app
arguments.desc: Set true to confirm plugging a source that already contains a cloudgrid.yaml as a NEW runtime app. On a create, if the source has a cloudgrid.yaml and this is not set, the result is needs_confirmation and nothing is created (target_entity_id re-plugs an existing entity instead).

arguments.name: filename
arguments.desc: Filename for the single-file `html` path. Defaults to index.html.

arguments.name: grid
arguments.desc: On create: the grid slug to plug into, chosen by the user. Omitted for a user with more than one grid, the result is needs_grid with the grid list to choose from; a single-grid user is not asked. The grid sets the new entity's URL, which members can see it, and its datastore tier and namespace. On re-plug the entity stays in its grid grids, but pass its home grid here when it differs from your active grid (the API checks your membership in the entity's grid). A drop plugged outside a grid stays outside until its owner claims it into one.

arguments.name: hints
arguments.desc: Classification hints for the CREATE path (not entity targeting, which is target_entity_id).

arguments.name: html
arguments.desc: A single self-contained HTML document to publish as an inspiration: the fast single-file path, live at a public URL in seconds. Pass the COMPLETE raw HTML inline (CSS+JS inline, images/fonts as data: URIs); a small fragment is wrapped into a full document. Raw text, not base64, and not an `@`-prefixed path or a file path. Mutually exclusive with `path` and `artifact_files`. Materialized as one index.html in the signed-in user's grid.

arguments.name: owner_token
arguments.desc: The owner token of a drop plugged outside a grid; it authorizes its re-plug (with target_entity_id). Re-minted on every such edit; the newest one from the result is the valid one.

arguments.name: slug
arguments.desc: Alternative RE-PLUG handle: paired with `grid`, resolves to an existing entity (the pickup contract's replug_handle) and updates it in place, for a client that holds only grid+slug, not the raw entity_id. target_entity_id takes precedence. A grid+slug that does NOT resolve to an existing entity is treated as a CREATE (not a false-positive re-plug).

arguments.name: target_entity_id
arguments.desc: Present → RE-PLUG: update this exact entity in place (same entity_id, slug, URL, plug history). Absent → CREATE a new entity. This is the durable handle a previous plug returned. Re-plugging a drop that was plugged outside a grid also needs its owner_token.

arguments.name: url
arguments.desc: Alternative RE-PLUG handle: the entity's public CloudGrid URL (e.g. https://<grid>.cloudgrid.io/<slug>) for editing in place with the URL and no target_entity_id (the common "change the color of this page" flow). The grid is read from the host and the entity is resolved via the pickup contract, so no `grid` param is needed. target_entity_id and grid+slug take precedence. A non-CloudGrid host is ignored (it does not redirect the write); a URL that does not resolve is treated as a CREATE.

annotations.title: Plug an app into the grid

name: grid_get_app_source
description: Returns the current HTML of a live page so it can be edited and re-plugged.

arguments.name: entity_id
arguments.desc: The drop's durable id, from its plug result. Enough on its own: its URL is looked up. Falls back to this session's last drop.

arguments.name: grid
arguments.desc: Grid slug, used only to construct the URL when neither url nor session state is available.

arguments.name: slug
arguments.desc: Entity slug, used with grid to construct the URL when neither url nor session state is available.

arguments.name: url
arguments.desc: The public URL of the drop (e.g. https://<grid>.cloudgrid.io/<slug>). Defaults to this session's last drop URL.

name: grid_visibility
description: Sets who can see a page or app: private, grid, link, or public.

arguments.name: entity_id
arguments.desc: The app's entity_id, from its plug result. Falls back to this session's last drop.

arguments.name: grid
arguments.desc: Grid of the entity. Defaults to the active grid.

arguments.name: indexed
arguments.desc: With visibility: link, makes the page search-engine indexable.

arguments.name: inside
arguments.desc: Axis 1, who in the grid can see it: private (only the user), spaces (selected spaces, listed in `spaces`), or grid (everyone in the grid). Use together with `outside`, instead of `visibility`.

arguments.name: kind
arguments.desc: Entity kind. Omit to auto-detect from this session's last drop (falls back to trying the runtime surface, then the inspiration surface).

arguments.name: org
arguments.desc: Legacy alias of grid.

arguments.name: outside
arguments.desc: Axis 2, reach beyond the grid: none, link (anyone with the link; add require_signin: true for signed-in accounts only), or public (anyone, and findable by search engines).

arguments.name: require_signin
arguments.desc: With outside: link (or visibility: link): the link requires a signed-in CloudGrid account.

arguments.name: spaces
arguments.desc: Space slugs, for inside: spaces (or the legacy space/grid modes).

arguments.name: target
arguments.desc: Legacy alias of entity_id.

arguments.name: url
arguments.desc: The app's public URL, when the entity_id is not at hand. Resolved to its entity_id.

arguments.name: visibility
arguments.desc: Simple mode: private | grid | link ('public' is an alias of link; indexed: true makes it search-findable; 'authenticated' is the retired alias for a sign-in-required link; 'space' needs the `spaces` list). Pass either this OR the inside/outside axes.

name: grid_check_deploy
description: Reports whether a runtime app's build has finished and the app is live.

arguments.name: entity_id
arguments.desc: The entity_id from the plug result. It finds the app's latest build. Falls back to this session's last plug.

arguments.name: grid
arguments.desc: Grid of the entity (the grid from the plug result). Defaults to the plug's grid, then the active grid.

arguments.name: poll_url
arguments.desc: The poll_url from a plug result, when it has one.

arguments.name: url
arguments.desc: The app's public URL, when the entity_id is not at hand (e.g. https://<slug>--<grid>.cloudgrid.io).

name: grid_list_grids
description: Lists the user's grids with name and role.

name: grid_start
description: Returns a short orientation and the workflow index.

name: grid_get_template
description: Loads a workflow, template, or reference doc by name.

arguments.name: kind
arguments.desc: What to fetch.

arguments.name: name
arguments.desc: The entry name, e.g. 'presentation' or 'deck'.

name: grid_report
description: Sends a failure report to the CloudGrid team, only after the user agrees.

arguments.name: message
arguments.desc: Short summary of what failed (required), not the whole conversation.

arguments.name: category
arguments.desc: Optional category, e.g. the failing tool name ("deploy"). Defaults to "mcp".

arguments.name: context
arguments.desc: The failed-request context. Redaction is key-name-only (a value is dropped only when its KEY looks secret) client-side, and the server applies the same key-name filter; a secret embedded in a value is not redacted by either.

arguments.name: failed_step
arguments.desc: The server-side pipeline step that failed, if known.

arguments.name: http_status
arguments.desc: The HTTP status of the final failed request, if applicable.

arguments.name: trace_id
arguments.desc: The server's trace/deploy id from the failed response, if any (helps support pivot to the trace).

name: grid_hello
description: Plugs a minimal hello page to check the account works.

arguments.name: grid
arguments.desc: Grid slug to plug into. Omitted for a user with several grids, the result lists them.

arguments.name: name
arguments.desc: Who to greet. Defaults to 'world'.

name: grid_delete
description: Takes a page offline; it needs explicit confirmation.

arguments.name: confirm
arguments.desc: Set to true to confirm; the call is refused without it.

arguments.name: name
arguments.desc: Entity slug to delete (required).

arguments.name: grid
arguments.desc: Grid slug to delete from. Omitted for a user with several grids, the result lists them.
